## Technical analysis (Sunday July 5, 2026 — US holiday, no session)

**No SPCX session.** US markets closed (Sunday). Last official close: $157.54 (July 2, Day 8). Reference: ~$162.00 (pre-market indication, not official).

**Step aside UNCHANGED. Updated framework summary:**
Bond distribution: Day 8 complete (~52M shares); Day 9 delayed again (triple closure July 3+4+5); resumes July 6. Clearance est. Day 11–12 (July 8–9). Re-entry gate: $185 (two consecutive closes) after clearance. $162 reference is $23 (−12.7%) below re-entry gate.

**Triple holiday impact:** Three consecutive US closures (July 3 abbreviated + July 4 Saturday + July 5 Sunday) have now pushed Day 9 two calendar days from the July 2 brief's original forecast. The total sessions remaining before clearance is unchanged (est. 3–4 sessions: Days 9, 10, then clearance Day 11–12), but the calendar dates are now July 6–9 rather than July 4–7. September 2 earnings timeline unchanged.

**IG floor buffer improvement:** Reference improved from $156.46 (July 2 session low, only $6.46 above $150 IG floor) to $162.00 ($12 above floor). The Korea-contagion scenario that threatened a holiday-gap IG floor test has been fully resolved (KOSPI +5.76% July 3, SK Hynix Stop Day 1 isolated, VIX at 15.78). July 6 opens with materially better IG floor protection.

**Day 9 volume estimate improvement:** The cross-asset risk-on backdrop (BTC Gate 2 + NVDA OTC above $195 + 62% upward July 6 open) reduces the probability of an elevated Day 9 seller surge. In a risk-on Monday open environment, fewer marginal sellers will press their distribution orders aggressively. Day 9 base case 25–30M revised slightly lower to 20–30M based on improved sentiment context. This could pull clearance forward by one session (Day 11 instead of Day 12).

**Inclusion day (Day 10) context update:** July 7 Nasdaq 100 inclusion (Day 10) arrives with VIX at 15.78 vs. June 26 Russell 1000 inclusion (Day 4) at VIX ~18. Lower VIX = higher risk appetite = potential for a larger and more sustained inclusion spike. Caveat: bond distribution sellers know the inclusion day and may specifically time their largest orders for Day 10 to sell into the $4.3B passive demand. The June 26 template remains the base case (spike absorbed, close below open), but a Day 10 close above $165–$170 is now within the plausible range.

**Key technical levels unchanged:** $185 re-entry gate is unchanged. $150 IG floor is unchanged. $162 reference puts SPCX in the 'distribution zone' between $150 and $185 — distribution mechanics are volume-driven, not technically-driven.
